facts.text: Thao legend says ancestors from the Jianan Plain, hunting in the Central Mountain Range, chased a rare white deer for days until it jumped into Sun Moon Lake.
The ancestors found the lake area rich in fish and good for farming, hunting and fishing, so they settled there.
Each Thao family keeps an ancestral spirit basket (ulalaluan) holding ancestors' clothing and ornaments.
The Thao believe their supreme ancestral spirit lives in a tree on Lalu Island.
Lalu is the most sacred ancestral place of the Thao.
A Thao cultural advisor has said that if Lalu disappeared, the Thao people would face the same fate.
Lalu is surrounded by floating docks and fields.
After the 921 Earthquake in 1999, the island formerly called Guanghua Island was renamed Lalu out of respect for the Thao.
The Thao population is less than 1,000 (about 817 people in January 2020).
Sun Moon Lake was turned into a large reservoir by the hydropower project; the First Power Plant was completed in 1934, during Japanese rule.
After the hydroelectric power plant flooded their area, the Thao were forced to move to Ita Thao (Barawbaw) Village.
In 2001, after a long effort, the government recognized the Thao as Taiwan's 10th Indigenous group.
Thao pestle music grew out of the rhythmic sound of pestles pounding grain and is performed by women of the village.
